tokens.v: Read the matte-black anodised device with the milled edges, machined side vent and knurled control that follows as this silver-top-plate rangefinder camera instead, and let the bench work on it: the dial indicator's chrome stand has been walked in until its plunger sits down on the top plate just behind the empty hot shoe, the needle swung a third off zero on a plain unnumbered face turned into frame, and that contact is the only place in the picture where two objects touch. 80mm at f/11 from sixty degrees above the granite, twenty-five centimetres out and square to the grid, so the whole top plate and both knurled dials open up and the body fills about two-thirds of the frame width, the fixed prime pointing camera-left with one bright line along its milled aperture ring. FIELDNOTE is engraved and paint-filled in clean capitals across the top plate, large and easily read at this magnification. The wrung gauge-block stack stands in the immediate foreground at frame-left, held tack sharp with the camera behind it, its corner cutting the bottom edge.
